page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor. This x86_64 architecture instance features 48 vCPUs, which correspond to 24 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 9 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong performance across multiple compute and memory tasks. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 65,056.32 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,030.0, both falling into the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 4,111.32 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 222.1 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In cryptographic and compression tests, the server demonstrated strong capabilities, with a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.16 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 310.53 GB/sec. For LLM inference, the server achieved top-tier performance on small 135M model text generation at 353.0 tokens per second, while maintaining strong performance on medium 7B models.

The c7i-flex.12xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads requiring high processing power without massive memory footprints. The lack of local storage means all storage must be network-attached, which may impact I/O-heavy applications depending on network conditions. The 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth is a potential constraint for highly distributed systems. However, the inclusion of advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) enhances its efficiency for vector and matrix operations. This makes the instance suitable for workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
